name: Report ad spend, cost per lead and return
summary: Reports each day what the business spends on Meta ads, what each ad costs per lead and how many leads it brings in, and queues a pause for any running ad over the owner's cost-per-lead limit. Return on ad spend needs the business's sales records, so that step stays with the owner. Crons read and draft; a person approves every pause.

all.evidence: 40 of 49 ad-reporting calls were read; 23 describe how they report, and most steps are done by hand

covered_by.pull-spend: draft (AdAccount insights and running ads, last 7 days)
covered_by.pull-leads: draft (lead counts from the insights actions, no contact details kept)
covered_by.calculate-cpl: cron (review: spend divided by leads, per ad and blended)
covered_by.calculate-return: skill (needs sales records the job does not read)
covered_by.compare-periods: skill (the store keeps one 7-day snapshot only)
covered_by.review-decide: skill (brand fit and which ads to keep or scale); cron pauses only ads over the limit
covered_by.adjust-campaigns: approval (a pause for an ad over the limit; budget changes are not built)
covered_by.record-keeping: draft (the snapshot and report kept in the workflow store)

crons.name: pull
crons.summary: Spend, leads and running ads for the last 7 days, kept for review (21:00 UTC is 7 or 8 am in eastern Australia).

crons.name: review
crons.summary: Writes the cost-per-lead report from the last pull and queues a pause for each running ad over the limit (22:00 UTC is 8 or 9 am in eastern Australia).

draft_ops_note: Draft operations are reads of the ad account. The only live operation is a pause of one ad (status PAUSED), which a cron can only queue and a person approves in the CRM shell.

meta-ads.covers: Ad-level spend, clicks, impressions and lead counts for the last 7 days; the list of running ads; a queued pause for one ad

gaps: Matching a lead to a later sale needs the business's own sales or CRM records. Meta's Conversions API only sends events from the business's systems, and the job does not read a sales system.
Return on ad spend is a judgment step. The job reports spend and cost per lead; the owner or agent works out return from the sales records.
Budget and bid changes (AdSet.post.self) are mapped in the kit but not built here. Scaling a winner stays with the owner.
Lead counts use Meta's lead action type. Leads tracked by the pixel under other action types are not counted; confirm in a live account.
Only the last 7 days are read, and only one snapshot is kept, so period-on-period comparison is not built.
The active-ads list is one page. When Meta returns a next page the report is marked partial, and a running ad past that page cannot be paused by this job.
Google Ads is mapped in the kit and appears in some calls, but this workflow has no Google Ads adapter because the platform evidence file does not list it for this job.
TikTok Ads has no operations mapped in the kit, so it has no adapter. Its reporting steps are in the platform evidence as partial, from TikTok's marketing pages only.
Roller, BigQuery and Looker Studio carry booking and dashboard data in the calls but are not mapped for this job. Build the report view in the business's own dashboard.
Google Sheets (record-keeping in some calls) is not mapped for this job; the workflow store holds the record.
Meta's ad rule history and preview (AdAccount.get.adrules_history, AdRule.post.preview) are mapped but not used; the pause rule is the owner's cost-per-lead limit.
The Meta token needs the ads read permission for reads and the ads management permission for the pause. Checked offline only, not against a real account.

evidence.calls: 49 ad-reporting calls for the all-industries workflow; 40 were read and 23 describe the process, with manual share at 100 percent on pull-spend, review-decide, compare-periods, adjust-campaigns and calculate-return
evidence.platforms: the Meta and TikTok Ads developer and marketing pages, mapped step by step; Meta has operations in the kit, TikTok does not
